headline: High-risk filesystem/network interaction: xonsh can read/write and egress broadly while Botpress may ingest trusted content, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or input provenance controls, while xonsh can read/write the filesystem and emit shell output. A shared file or copied output could be treated as trusted instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty escalation.
conditions: IF Botpress ingests xonsh-produced file content as instructions or context, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a workspace or copied transcript, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by xonsh.
Require explicit human review before Botpress acts on external text.
Use a provenance tag on all xonsh outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh reads filesystem contents and environment variables and has broad network egress, while Botpress is a support agent with no documented data-class restrictions. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive files can flow from xonsh into Botpress prompts or outputs. The evidence is indirect, but the shared-file pathway is credible enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory, xonsh can expose files that Botpress later summarizes.
IF Botpress forwards user content to external services, any shared sensitive file content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts.
Restrict xonsh to non-sensitive paths.
Review Botpress prompts for file attachments before use.
Turn off any external forwarding for sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Botpress can install packages. Even without direct overlap in write permissions, both can mutate local state through different mechanisms, so concurrent use can conflict on shared files or environments. The profiles do not show locking, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working tree, file clobbering can occur.
IF Botpress installs or updates dependencies while xonsh is running, environment drift can break tasks.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent package changes.
Freeze dependencies before running both agents.
Use a lockfile or wrapper script.
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a support agent that may turn xonsh-generated text into user-facing responses, while xonsh can emit arbitrary shell output. If Botpress treats that output as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so medium fits the default-risk pathway.
conditions: IF Botpress uses xonsh output as source material without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Botpress triggers actions based on xonsh command results, a bad command can cascade into user-visible errors.
mitigations: Require Botpress to cite and verify xonsh outputs.
Add a human approval step for consequential actions.
Limit xonsh to read-only commands for shared workflows.
Log command provenance alongside outputs.
requires-engineering: implement structured-result validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Botpress is open-source and xonsh is local shell tooling, so the compliance pathway is not evidenced beyond general deployment risk. I therefore keep this low rather than medium, and I do not need a separate citation for the other agent because no concrete mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF a deployment routes regulated data through a non-compliant Botpress hosting setup, compliance risk appears.
IF xonsh is run outside the intended isolated environment, local policy controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of unsupported hosting.
Run xonsh only inside its isolated environment.
Document retention and deletion settings.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review for the deployment.
